Reading the room

  • Your 120 cm floor removes most of IKEA’s round range. Searching a 315-product pool, IKEA sells exactly five round tables at 120 cm or over: NÄSINGE, SKOGSTA, MÖRBYLÅNGA and the two extendables. Round and big is where IKEA stops and Sklum starts.
  • The two pendants are the constraint nobody mentions. They hang in a line, spaced for a long table. That is an argument for a rectangle: a round table wants one light centred over it, and you have two.
  • At 120 cm a rectangle beats a circle on floor. A Ø120 circle and a 120×80 rectangle seat the same four people, but the rectangle sits against a wall and leaves you a walkway. The circle has to live in the middle of the room.
  • Match the floor or contrast it, never near-miss it. Your laminate is a pale grey-toned oak. Acacia, walnut and brown-stained oak read warmer and redder, which works as a deliberate contrast. An oak veneer one shade off reads as a mistake.
  • Only the pendants are black. A table with a black frame or leg (SKOGSTA, TARSELE, MARIEDAMM, the black-legged SKÅLSTA) is the one thing that would answer them.
  • Sklum ships from Spain and several pieces are on back-order — the card says which. Check the delivery window before committing.
Prices, sizes and stock read live on Saturday 29 August 2026: IKEA from its UK search and stock APIs, Sklum from product data on all 94 of its dining tables. Sizes are the longest published dimension — diameter for round, length for rectangular; an extending table is filed under its open size and marked extends.

Habitat cards say check price because habitat.co.uk and argos.co.uk block automated requests outright — HTML, their internal API, a headless browser and a server-side fetch all return 403. Only their image CDN answers, so those cards carry real photographs and sizes but no price. John Lewis, Dunelm, Wayfair, La Redoute, Made, Heal’s and Furniture Village were tried and are blocked or fully client-side.
